author: Lao Tzu

quote: There is an invisible strength within us; when it recognizes two opposing objects of desire, it grows stronger.
author: Rumi

quote: He who conquers others is strong He who conquers himself is mighty.
author: Lao Tzu

quote: We gain the strength of the temptation we resist.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: Because your own strength is unequal to the task, do not assume that it is beyond the powers of man; but if anything is within the powers and province of man, believe that it is within your own compass also.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Simulated disorder postulates perfect discipline simulated fear postulates courage simulated weakness postulates strength.
author: Lao Tzu

quote: The strength of a man's virtue should not be measured by his special exertions, but by his habitual acts.
author: Blaise Pascal

quote: Peace is not the absence of war, but a virtue based on strength of character.
author: Baruch Spinoza

quote: Atheism shows strength of mind, but only to a certain degree.
author: Blaise Pascal

quote: The relationship to one's fellow man is the relationship of prayer, the relationship to oneself is the relationship of striving; it is from prayer that one draws the strength for one's striving.
author: Franz Kafka

quote: I have just three things to teach: simplicity, patience, compassion. These three are your greatest treasures.
author: Lao Tzu

quote: Death may be the greatest of all human blessings.
author: Socrates

quote: Life and death are one thread, the same line viewed from different sides.
author: Lao Tzu

quote: Without health life is not life it is only a state of langour and suffering - an image of death.
author: Buddha

quote: God is dead. God remains dead. And we have killed him. Yet his shadow still looms. How shall we comfort ourselves, the murderers of all murderers? What was holiest and mightiest of all that the world has yet owned has bled to death under our knives; who will wipe this blood off us? What water is there for us to clean ourselves?
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: Regard your soldiers as your children, and they will follow you into the deepest valleys; look on them as your own beloved sons, and they will stand by you even unto death.
author: Sun Tzu

quote: Even death is not to be feared by one who has lived wisely.
author: Buddha

quote: If I take death into my life, acknowledge it, and face it squarely, I will free myself from the anxiety of death and the pettiness of life - and only then will I be free to become myself.
author: Martin Heidegger

quote: If we don't know life, how can we know death?
author: Confucius

quote: To be idle is a short road to death and to be diligent is a way of life; foolish people are idle, wise people are diligent.
author: Buddha

quote: No evil can happen to a good man, either in life or after death.
author: Plato

quote: Death comes to all, but great achievements build a monument which shall endure until the sun grows cold.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: To run away from trouble is a form of cowardice and, while it is true that the suicide braves death, he does it not for some noble object but to escape some ill.
author: Aristotle

quote: Death and life have their determined appointments riches and honors depend upon heaven.
author: Confucius

quote: Ordinary people seem not to realize that those who really apply themselves in the right way to philosophy are directly and of their own accord preparing themselves for dying and death.
author: Socrates

quote: The 'kingdom of Heaven' is a condition of the heart - not something that comes 'upon the earth' or 'after death.'
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: Prohibit the taking of omens, and do away with superstitious doubts. Then, until death itself comes, no calamity need be feared.
author: Sun Tzu

quote: One is still what one is going to cease to be and already what one is going to become. One lives one's death, one dies one's life.
author: Jean-Paul Sartre

quote: Pale Death beats equally at the poor man's gate and at the palaces of kings.
author: Horace

quote: Good is positive. Evil is merely privative, not absolute: it is like cold, which is the privation of heat. All evil is so much death or nonentity. Benevolence is absolute and real. So much benevolence as a man hath, so much life hath he.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: Do the thing we fear, and death of fear is certain.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: Death is a release from the impressions of the senses, and from desires that make us their puppets, and from the vagaries of the mind, and from the hard service of the flesh.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: It is old age, rather than death, that is to be contrasted with life. Old age is life's parody, whereas death transforms life into a destiny: in a way it preserves it by giving it the absolute dimension. Death does away with time.
author: Simone de Beauvoir

quote: Death is not the worst that can happen to men.
author: Plato

quote: Just as I shall select my ship when I am about to go on a voyage, or my house when I propose to take a residence, so I shall choose my death when I am about to depart from life.
author: Seneca

quote: I am not made for politics because I am incapable of wanting or accepting the death of the adversary.
author: Albert Camus

quote: For centuries the death penalty, often accompanied by barbarous refinements, has been trying to hold crime in check; yet crime persists. Why? Because the instincts that are warring in man are not, as the law claims, constant forces in a state of equilibrium.
author: Albert Camus

quote: The charm of fame is so great that we like every object to which it is attached, even death.
author: Blaise Pascal

quote: In order to speak about all and to all, one has to speak of what all know and of the reality common to us all. The sea, rains, necessity, desire, the struggle against death... these are things that unite us all.
author: Albert Camus

quote: Birth was the death of him.
author: Samuel Beckett

quote: Know one knows whether death, which people fear to be the greatest evil, may not be the greatest good.
author: Plato

quote: It is not death or pain that is to be dreaded, but the fear of pain or death.
author: Epictetus

quote: It is possible to provide security against other ills, but as far as death is concerned, we men live in a city without walls.
author: Epicurus

quote: The worst form of inequality is to try to make unequal things equal.
author: Aristotle

quote: Democracy... is a charming form of government, full of variety and disorder; and dispensing a sort of equality to equals and unequals alike.
author: Plato

quote: If liberty and equality, as is thought by some, are chiefly to be found in democracy, they will be best attained when all persons alike share in government to the utmost.
author: Aristotle

quote: Then not only custom, but also nature affirms that to do is more disgraceful than to suffer injustice, and that justice is equality.
author: Plato

quote: Good habits formed at youth make all the difference.
author: Aristotle

quote: Music is a moral law. It gives soul to the universe, wings to the mind, flight to the imagination, and charm and gaiety to life and to everything.
author: Plato

quote: Music is the movement of sound to reach the soul for the education of its virtue.
author: Plato

quote: How to play music may be known. At the commencement of the piece, all the parts should sound together. As it proceeds, they should be in harmony while severally distinct and flowing without break, and thus on to the conclusion.
author: Confucius

quote: Those who have virtue always in their mouths, and neglect it in practice, are like a harp, which emits a sound pleasing to others, while itself is insensible of the music.
author: Diogenes

quote: One and the same thing can at the same time be good, bad, and indifferent, e.g., music is good to the melancholy, bad to those who mourn, and neither good nor bad to the deaf.
author: Baruch Spinoza

quote: Is Wagner a human being at all? Is he not rather a disease? He contaminates everything he touches - he has made music sick.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: For the introduction of a new kind of music must be shunned as imperiling the whole state since styles of music are never disturbed without affecting the most important political institutions.
author: Plato

quote: The age of a woman doesn't mean a thing. The best tunes are played on the oldest fiddles.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: When marrying, ask yourself this question: Do you believe that you will be able to converse well with this person into your old age? Everything else in marriage is transitory.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: Education is the best provision for old age.
author: Aristotle

quote: Old age, believe me, is a good and pleasant thing. It is true you are gently shouldered off the stage, but then you are given such a comfortable front stall as spectator.
author: Confucius

quote: Alas, after a certain age every man is responsible for his face.
author: Albert Camus

quote: Bashfulness is an ornament to youth, but a reproach to old age.
author: Aristotle

quote: Let no one be slow to seek wisdom when he is young nor weary in the search of it when he has grown old. For no age is too early or too late for the health of the soul.
author: Epicurus

quote: All diseases run into one, old age.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: Each age, it is found, must write its own books; or rather, each generation for the next succeeding.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: Every age has its own poetry; in every age the circumstances of history choose a nation, a race, a class to take up the torch by creating situations that can be expressed or transcended only through poetry.
author: Jean-Paul Sartre

quote: What is an adult? A child blown up by age.
author: Simone de Beauvoir

quote: To enjoy good health, to bring true happiness to one's family, to bring peace to all, one must first discipline and control one's own mind. If a man can control his mind he can find the way to Enlightenment, and all wisdom and virtue will naturally come to him.
author: Buddha

quote: There is only one way to happiness and that is to cease worrying about things which are beyond the power of our will.
author: Epictetus

quote: Morality is not the doctrine of how we may make ourselves happy, but how we may make ourselves worthy of happiness.
author: Immanuel Kant

quote: Happiness is not an ideal of reason, but of imagination.
author: Immanuel Kant

quote: They must often change, who would be constant in happiness or wisdom.
author: Confucius

quote: Different men seek after happiness in different ways and by different means, and so make for themselves different modes of life and forms of government.
author: Aristotle

quote: But what is happiness except the simple harmony between a man and the life he leads?
author: Albert Camus

quote: All happiness or unhappiness solely depends upon the quality of the object to which we are attached by love.
author: Baruch Spinoza

quote: Happiness is neither without us nor within us. It is in God, both without us and within us.
author: Blaise Pascal

quote: Heroism is accessible. Happiness is more difficult.
author: Albert Camus

quote: We must exercise ourselves in the things which bring happiness, since, if that be present, we have everything, and, if that be absent, all our actions are directed toward attaining it.
author: Epicurus

quote: In theory there is a possibility of perfect happiness: To believe in the indestructible element within one, and not to strive towards it.
author: Franz Kafka

quote: Action may not bring happiness but there is no happiness without action.
author: William James

quote: Happiness is a virtue, not its reward.
author: Baruch Spinoza

quote: It is not God's will merely that we should be happy, but that we should make ourselves happy.
author: Immanuel Kant

quote: Such happiness as life is capable of comes from the full participation of all our powers in the endeavor to wrest from each changing situations of experience its own full and unique meaning.
author: John Dewey

quote: How to gain, how to keep, how to recover happiness is in fact for most men at all times the secret motive of all they do, and of all they are willing to endure.
author: William James

quote: If virtue promises happiness, prosperity and peace, then progress in virtue is progress in each of these for to whatever point the perfection of anything brings us, progress is always an approach toward it.
author: Epictetus

quote: We find delight in the beauty and happiness of children that makes the heart too big for the body.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: Imagination disposes of everything; it creates beauty, justice, and happiness, which are everything in this world.
author: Blaise Pascal

quote: Politicians also have no leisure, because they are always aiming at something beyond political life itself, power and glory, or happiness.
author: Aristotle

quote: Your successes and happiness are forgiven you only if you generously consent to share them.
author: Albert Camus

quote: You traverse the world in search of happiness, which is within the reach of every man. A contented mind confers it on all.
author: Horace

quote: The sun is new each day.
author: Heraclitus

quote: In the morning a man walks with his whole body; in the evening, only with his legs.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: There is no great genius without some touch of madness.
author: Aristotle

quote: Common sense is genius dressed in its working clothes.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: An intellectual is someone whose mind watches itself.
author: Albert Camus

quote: If you would take, you must first give, this is the beginning of intelligence.
author: Lao Tzu

quote: Immaturity is the incapacity to use one's intelligence without the guidance of another.
author: Immanuel Kant

quote: Man is the most intelligent of the animals - and the most silly.
author: Diogenes

quote: It is only the enlightened ruler and the wise general who will use the highest intelligence of the army for the purposes of spying, and thereby they achieve great results.
author: Sun Tzu

quote: The modern mind is in complete disarray. Knowledge has stretched itself to the point where neither the world nor our intelligence can find any foot-hold. It is a fact that we are suffering from nihilism.
author: Albert Camus

quote: Genius always finds itself a century too early.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: Ah! yes, I know: those who see me rarely trust my word: I must look too intelligent to keep it.
author: Jean-Paul Sartre

quote: Poets are the sense, philosophers the intelligence of humanity.
author: Samuel Beckett

quote: The heart has its reasons of which reason knows nothing.
author: Blaise Pascal

quote: He who learns but does not think, is lost! He who thinks but does not learn is in great danger.
author: Confucius

quote: He who would learn to fly one day must first learn to stand and walk and run and climb and dance one cannot fly into flying.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: Much learning does not teach understanding.
author: Heraclitus

quote: Learning without thought is labor lost thought without learning is perilous.
author: Confucius

quote: Ignorance of all things is an evil neither terrible nor excessive, nor yet the greatest of all; but great cleverness and much learning, if they be accompanied by a bad training, are a much greater misfortune.
author: Plato

quote: The learning and knowledge that we have, is, at the most, but little compared with that of which we are ignorant.
author: Plato

quote: We do not learn and what we call learning is only a process of recollection.
author: Plato

quote: I would fain grow old learning many things.
author: Plato

quote: The only real progress lies in learning to be wrong all alone.
author: Albert Camus

quote: Entire ignorance is not so terrible or extreme an evil, and is far from being the greatest of all; too much cleverness and too much learning, accompanied with ill bringing-up, are far more fatal.
author: Plato

quote: No man ever prayed heartily without learning something.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: So long as you have food in your mouth, you have solved all questions for the time being.
author: Franz Kafka

quote: Agriculture is now a motorized food industry, the same thing in its essence as the production of corpses in the gas chambers and the extermination camps, the same thing as blockades and the reduction of countries to famine, the same thing as the manufacture of hydrogen bombs.
author: Martin Heidegger

quote: And what, Socrates, is the food of the soul? Surely, I said, knowledge is the food of the soul.
author: Plato

quote: What is food to one man is bitter poison to others.
author: Lucretius

quote: I would rather live my life as if there is a God and die to find out there isn't, than live as if there isn't and to die to find out that there is.
author: Albert Camus

quote: God is a thought who makes crooked all that is straight.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: Only a god can save us.
author: Martin Heidegger

quote: There is not enough religion in the world even to destroy religion.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: All religions must be tolerated... for every man must get to heaven in his own way.
author: Epictetus

quote: Religion is the recognition of all our duties as divine commands.
author: Immanuel Kant

quote: Human beings must be known to be loved but Divine beings must be loved to be known.
author: Blaise Pascal

quote: If we must not act save on a certainty, we ought not to act on religion, for it is not certain. But how many things we do on an uncertainty, sea voyages, battles!
author: Blaise Pascal

quote: So potent was religion in persuading to evil deeds.
author: Lucretius

quote: I was born poor and without religion, under a happy sky, feeling harmony, not hostility, in nature. I began not by feeling torn, but in plenitude.
author: Albert Camus

quote: Unless we place our religion and our treasure in the same thing, religion will always be sacrificed.
author: Epictetus

quote: Such are the heights of wickedness to which men are driven by religion.
author: Lucretius

quote: Only the guy who isn't rowing has time to rock the boat.
author: Jean-Paul Sartre

quote: Anybody can become angry - that is easy, but to be angry with the right person and to the right degree and at the right time and for the right purpose, and in the right way - that is not within everybody's power and is not easy.
author: Aristotle

quote: All things are subject to interpretation whichever interpretation prevails at a given time is a function of power and not truth.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: Our greatest glory is not in never failing, but in rising up every time we fail.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: We live in deeds, not years; in thoughts, not breaths; in feelings, not in figures on a dial. We should count time by heart throbs. He most lives who thinks most, feels the noblest, acts the best.
author: Aristotle

quote: I am not the first Buddha who came upon Earth, nor shall I be the last. In due time, another Buddha will arise in the world - a Holy One, a supremely enlightened One, endowed with wisdom in conduct, auspicious, knowing the universe, an incomparable leader of men, a master of angels and mortals.
author: Buddha

quote: Time itself comes in drops.
author: William James

quote: Time and memory are true artists they remould reality nearer to the heart's desire.
author: John Dewey

quote: We name time when we say: every thing has its time. This means: everything which actually is, every being comes and goes at the right time and remains for a time during the time allotted to it. Every thing has its time.
author: Martin Heidegger

quote: The most thought-provoking thing in our thought-provoking time is that we are still not thinking.
author: Martin Heidegger

quote: Employ your time in improving yourself by other men's writings, so that you shall gain easily what others have labored hard for.
author: Socrates

quote: Nothing great is created suddenly, any more than a bunch of grapes or a fig. If you tell me that you desire a fig. I answer you that there must be time. Let it first blossom, then bear fruit, then ripen.
author: Epictetus

quote: Time is a sort of river of passing events, and strong is its current; no sooner is a thing brought to sight than it is swept by and another takes its place, and this too will be swept away.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: How much time he saves who does not look to see what his neighbor says or does or thinks.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: True time is four-dimensional.
author: Martin Heidegger

quote: Conscious of not being able to separate myself from my time, I have decided to become part of it.
author: Albert Camus

quote: Ah, women. They make the highs higher and the lows more frequent.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: Nothing can be more absurd than the practice that prevails in our country of men and women not following the same pursuits with all their strengths and with one mind, for thus, the state instead of being whole is reduced to half.
author: Plato

quote: Women are considered deep - why? Because one can never discover any bottom to them. Women are not even shallow.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: If I became a philosopher, if I have so keenly sought this fame for which I'm still waiting, it's all been to seduce women basically.
author: Jean-Paul Sartre

quote: Genteel women suppose that those things do not really exist about which it is impossible to talk in polite company.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: The most mediocre of males feels himself a demigod as compared with women.
author: Simone de Beauvoir

quote: Behind all their personal vanity, women themselves always have an impersonal contempt for woman.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: Stupid as a man, say the women: cowardly as a woman, say the men. Stupidity in a woman is unwomanly.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: The key is to keep company only with people who uplift you, whose presence calls forth your best.
author: Epictetus

quote: My best friend is the man who in wishing me well wishes it for my sake.
author: Aristotle

quote: At his best, man is the noblest of all animals; separated from law and justice he is the worst.
author: Aristotle

quote: The ideal man bears the accidents of life with dignity and grace, making the best of circumstances.
author: Aristotle

quote: The best work is not what is most difficult for you it is what you do best.
author: Jean-Paul Sartre

quote: The fox has many tricks. The hedgehog has but one. But that is the best of all.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: Make the best use of what is in your power, and take the rest as it happens.
author: Epictetus

quote: To refrain from imitation is the best revenge.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: The best effort of a fine person is felt after we have left their presence.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: Our best thoughts come from others.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: A good traveler has no fixed plans, and is not intent on arriving.
author: Lao Tzu

quote: To keep the body in good health is a duty... otherwise we shall not be able to keep our mind strong and clear.
author: Buddha

quote: It is easy to hate and it is difficult to love. This is how the whole scheme of things works. All good things are difficult to achieve and bad things are very easy to get.
author: Confucius

quote: Just as treasures are uncovered from the earth, so virtue appears from good deeds, and wisdom appears from a pure and peaceful mind. To walk safely through the maze of human life, one needs the light of wisdom and the guidance of virtue.
author: Buddha

quote: A good decision is based on knowledge and not on numbers.
author: Plato

quote: By all means, marry. If you get a good wife, you'll become happy; if you get a bad one, you'll become a philosopher.
author: Socrates

quote: When one has not had a good father, one must create one.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: Treat those who are good with goodness, and also treat those who are not good with goodness. Thus goodness is attained. Be honest to those who are honest, and be also honest to those who are not honest. Thus honesty is attained.
author: Lao Tzu

quote: A good commander is benevolent and unconcerned with fame.
author: Sun Tzu

quote: We are all ready to be savage in some cause. The difference between a good man and a bad one is the choice of the cause.
author: William James

quote: Persuasion is achieved by the speaker's personal character when the speech is so spoken as to make us think him credible. We believe good men more fully and more readily than others: this is true generally whatever the question is, and absolutely true where exact certainty is impossible and opinions are divided.
author: Aristotle

quote: The evil that is in the world almost always comes of ignorance, and good intentions may do as much harm as malevolence if they lack understanding.
author: Albert Camus

quote: It takes more than just a good looking body. You've got to have the heart and soul to go with it.
author: Epictetus

quote: The general who advances without coveting fame and retreats without fearing disgrace, whose only thought is to protect his country and do good service for his sovereign, is the jewel of the kingdom.
author: Sun Tzu

quote: The aim of a college education is to teach you to know a good man when you see one.
author: William James

quote: Not life, but good life, is to be chiefly valued.
author: Socrates

quote: Doing well is the result of doing good. That's what capitalism is all about.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: Virtue is persecuted more by the wicked than it is loved by the good.
author: Buddha

quote: We ought to do good to others as simply as a horse runs, or a bee makes honey, or a vine bears grapes season after season without thinking of the grapes it has borne.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Whoever does not have a good father should procure one.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: Jealousy is both reasonable and belongs to reasonable men, while envy is base and belongs to the base, for the one makes himself get good things by jealousy, while the other does not allow his neighbour to have them through envy.
author: Aristotle

quote: Twice and thrice over, as they say, good is it to repeat and review what is good.
author: Plato

quote: Of all that is good, sublimity is supreme. Succeeding is the coming together of all that is beautiful. Furtherance is the agreement of all that is just. Perseverance is the foundation of all actions.
author: Lao Tzu

quote: When one has the feeling of dislike for evil, when one feels tranquil, one finds pleasure in listening to good teachings; when one has these feelings and appreciates them, one is free of fear.
author: Buddha

quote: It is not good to be too free. It is not good to have everything one wants.
author: Blaise Pascal

quote: Here is the rule to remember in the future, When anything tempts you to be bitter: not, 'This is a misfortune' but 'To bear this worthily is good fortune.'
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: A heart well prepared for adversity in bad times hopes, and in good times fears for a change in fortune.
author: Horace

quote: As a matter of self-preservation, a man needs good friends or ardent enemies, for the former instruct him and the latter take him to task.
author: Diogenes

quote: A good indignation brings out all one's powers.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: What I like to drink most is wine that belongs to others.
author: Diogenes

quote: Man is not logical and his intellectual history is a record of mental reserves and compromises. He hangs on to what he can in his old beliefs even when he is compelled to surrender their logical basis.
author: John Dewey

quote: Jesus Christ belonged to the true race of prophets. He saw with open eye the mystery of the soul. Drawn by its severe harmony, ravished with its beauty, he lived in it and had his being there. Alone in all history, he estimated the greatness of man.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: To correct a natural indifference I was placed half-way between misery and the sun. Misery kept me from believing that all was well under the sun, and the sun taught me that history wasn't everything.
author: Albert Camus

quote: The history of mankind is the instant between two strides taken by a traveler.
author: Franz Kafka

quote: But every historical statement and legitimization itself moves within a certain relation to history.
author: Martin Heidegger

quote: In the course of history, men come to see that iron necessity is neither iron nor necessary.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: Pessimism leads to weakness, optimism to power.
author: William James

quote: There will be no end to the troubles of states, or of humanity itself, till philosophers become kings in this world, or till those we now call kings and rulers really and truly become philosophers, and political power and philosophy thus come into the same hands.
author: Plato

quote: The ultimate value of life depends upon awareness and the power of contemplation rather than upon mere survival.
author: Aristotle

quote: Balk the enemy's power force him to reveal himself.
author: Sun Tzu

quote: What it lies in our power to do, it lies in our power not to do.
author: Aristotle

quote: I only wish that ordinary people had an unlimited capacity for doing harm then they might have an unlimited power for doing good.
author: Socrates

quote: It is folly for a man to pray to the gods for that which he has the power to obtain by himself.
author: Epicurus

quote: In a democracy the poor will have more power than the rich, because there are more of them, and the will of the majority is supreme.
author: Aristotle

quote: To give aid to every poor man is far beyond the reach and power of every man. Care of the poor is incumbent on society as a whole.
author: Baruch Spinoza

quote: I assess the power of a will by how much resistance, pain, torture it endures and knows how to turn to its advantage.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: And so it is, that both the Devil and the angelic Spirit present us with objects of desire to awaken our power of choice.
author: Rumi

quote: To live happily is an inward power of the soul.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Justice and power must be brought together, so that whatever is just may be powerful, and whatever is powerful may be just.
author: Blaise Pascal

quote: The world itself is the will to power - and nothing else! And you yourself are the will to power - and nothing else!
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: Ambition is the immoderate desire for power.
author: Baruch Spinoza

quote: What is good? All that heightens the feeling of power, the will to power, power itself in man.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: Man's greatness lies in his power of thought.
author: Blaise Pascal

quote: Not necessity, not desire - no, the love of power is the demon of men. Let them have everything - health, food, a place to live, entertainment - they are and remain unhappy and low-spirited: for the demon waits and waits and will be satisfied.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: Freedom is nothing but a chance to be better.
author: Albert Camus

quote: There is no chance and anarchy in the universe. All is system and gradation. Every god is there sitting in his sphere.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: There are people who want to make men's lives more difficult for no other reason than the chance it provides them afterwards to offer their prescription for alleviating life; their Christianity, for instance.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: Chance gives rise to thoughts, and chance removes them; no art can keep or acquire them.
author: Blaise Pascal

quote: It is just that we should be grateful, not only to those with whose views we may agree, but also to those who have expressed more superficial views; for these also contributed something, by developing before us the powers of thought.
author: Aristotle

quote: Never lose an opportunity of seeing anything beautiful, for beauty is God's handwriting.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: Woman is a ray of God. She is not that earthly beloved: she is creative, not created.
author: Rumi

quote: Whosoever is delighted in solitude is either a wild beast or a god.
author: Aristotle

quote: God is the indwelling and not the transient cause of all things.
author: Baruch Spinoza

author: John Dewey

quote: To accuse others for one's own misfortunes is a sign of want of education. To accuse oneself shows that one's education has begun. To accuse neither oneself nor others shows that one's education is complete.
author: Epictetus

quote: The direction in which education starts a man will determine his future in life.
author: Plato

quote: Since we cannot know all that there is to be known about anything, we ought to know a little about everything.
author: Blaise Pascal

quote: Natural ability without education has more often raised a man to glory and virtue than education without natural ability.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: The most important part of education is proper training in the nursery.
author: Plato

quote: In large states public education will always be mediocre, for the same reason that in large kitchens the cooking is usually bad.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: The journey of a thousand miles begins with one step.
author: Lao Tzu

quote: When it is obvious that the goals cannot be reached, don't adjust the goals, adjust the action steps.
author: Confucius

quote: Knowing others is wisdom, knowing yourself is Enlightenment.
author: Lao Tzu

quote: Be as you wish to seem.
author: Socrates

quote: Commitment is an act, not a word.
author: Jean-Paul Sartre

quote: True wisdom comes to each of us when we realize how little we understand about life, ourselves, and the world around us.
author: Socrates

quote: It's not what happens to you, but how you react to it that matters.
author: Epictetus

quote: Wisdom begins in wonder.
author: Socrates

quote: There is more wisdom in your body than in your deepest philosophy.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: There are three classes of men; lovers of wisdom, lovers of honor, and lovers of gain.
author: Plato

quote: I decided that it was not wisdom that enabled poets to write their poetry, but a kind of instinct or inspiration, such as you find in seers and prophets who deliver all their sublime messages without knowing in the least what they mean.
author: Socrates

quote: He who lives in harmony with himself lives in harmony with the universe.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Let my skin and sinews and bones dry up, together with all the flesh and blood of my body! I welcome it! But I will not move from this spot until I have attained the supreme and final wisdom.
author: Buddha

quote: Both old and young alike ought to seek wisdom: the former in order that, as age comes over him, he may be young in good things because of the grace of what has been, and the latter in order that, while he is young, he may at the same time be old, because he has no fear of the things which are to come.
author: Epicurus

quote: Does wisdom perhaps appear on the earth as a raven which is inspired by the smell of carrion?
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: Start with what is right rather than what is acceptable.
author: Franz Kafka

quote: Wise kings generally have wise counselors and he must be a wise man himself who is capable of distinguishing one.
author: Diogenes

quote: Cunning... is but the low mimic of wisdom.
author: Plato

quote: The sum of wisdom is that time is never lost that is devoted to work.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: The virtue of justice consists in moderation, as regulated by wisdom.
author: Aristotle

quote: Before we acquire great power we must acquire wisdom to use it well.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: The fall of dropping water wears away the Stone.
author: Lucretius

quote: Wisdom has its root in goodness, not goodness its root in wisdom.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: Excellence, then, is a state concerned with choice, lying in a mean, relative to us, this being determined by reason and in the way in which the man of practical wisdom would determine it.
author: Aristotle

quote: Wisdom is not wisdom when it is derived from books alone.
author: Horace

quote: For every minute you remain angry, you give up sixty seconds of peace of mind.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: Peace comes from within. Do not seek it without.
author: Buddha

quote: Those who are free of resentful thoughts surely find peace.
author: Buddha

quote: Better than a thousand hollow words, is one word that brings peace.
author: Buddha

quote: Nobody can bring you peace but yourself.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: Do not overrate what you have received, nor envy others. He who envies others does not obtain peace of mind.
author: Buddha

quote: Nowhere can man find a quieter or more untroubled retreat than in his own soul.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: One can not reflect in streaming water. Only those who know internal peace can give it to others.
author: Lao Tzu

quote: Do not dwell in the past, do not dream of the future, concentrate the mind on the present moment.
author: Buddha

quote: Very little is needed to make a happy life; it is all within yourself, in your way of thinking.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Life is a series of natural and spontaneous changes. Don't resist them - that only creates sorrow. Let reality be reality. Let things flow naturally forward in whatever way they like.
author: Lao Tzu

quote: Beware the barrenness of a busy life.
author: Socrates

quote: He who has a why to live can bear almost any how.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: All life is an experiment. The more experiments you make the better.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: A chain is no stronger than its weakest link, and life is after all a chain.
author: William James

quote: Why should we think upon things that are lovely? Because thinking determines life. It is a common habit to blame life upon the environment. Environment modifies life but does not govern life. The soul is stronger than its surroundings.
author: William James

quote: It is not length of life, but depth of life.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: Life must be lived as play.
author: Plato

quote: Everything has been figured out, except how to live.
author: Jean-Paul Sartre

quote: With the past, I have nothing to do; nor with the future. I live now.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: Execute every act of thy life as though it were thy last.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Begin at once to live, and count each separate day as a separate life.
author: Seneca

quote: This life is worth living, we can say, since it is what we make it.
author: William James

quote: Life is a succession of lessons which must be lived to be understood. All is riddle, and the key to a riddle is another riddle.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: Life consists in what a man is thinking of all day.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: Life is largely a matter of expectation.
author: Horace

quote: Remember when life's path is steep to keep your mind even.
author: Horace

quote: The greatest use of a life is to spend it on something that will outlast it.
author: William James

quote: He who loves 50 people has 50 woes he who loves no one has no woes.
author: Buddha

quote: Adapt yourself to the things among which your lot has been cast and love sincerely the fellow creatures with whom destiny has ordained that you shall live.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Invincibility lies in the defence the possibility of victory in the attack.
author: Sun Tzu

quote: The superior man makes the difficulty to be overcome his first interest success only comes later.
author: Confucius

quote: One man cannot practice many arts with success.
author: Plato

quote: Forward, as occasion offers. Never look round to see whether any shall note it... Be satisfied with success in even the smallest matter, and think that even such a result is no trifle.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Not every difficult and dangerous thing is suitable for training, but only that which is conducive to success in achieving the object of our effort.
author: Epictetus

quote: Hence poetry is something more philosophic and of graver import than history, since its statements are rather of the nature of universals, whereas those of history are singulars.
author: Aristotle

quote: No poems can please for long or live that are written by water drinkers.
author: Horace

quote: A hero is born among a hundred, a wise man is found among a thousand, but an accomplished one might not be found even among a hundred thousand men.
author: Plato

quote: Victory usually goes to the army who has better trained officers and men.
author: Sun Tzu

quote: All men's miseries derive from not being able to sit in a quiet room alone.
author: Blaise Pascal

quote: All men's souls are immortal, but the souls of the righteous are immortal and divine.
author: Socrates

quote: It disturbs me no more to find men base, unjust, or selfish than to see apes mischievous, wolves savage, or the vulture ravenous.
author: Jean-Paul Sartre

quote: I have often wondered how it is that every man loves himself more than all the rest of men, but yet sets less value on his own opinions of himself than on the opinions of others.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: All men can see these tactics whereby I conquer, but what none can see is the strategy out of which victory is evolved.
author: Sun Tzu

quote: I do not believe in a fate that falls on men however they act but I do believe in a fate that falls on them unless they act.
author: Buddha

quote: Let men see, let them know, a real man, who lives as he was meant to live.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: The superior man is distressed by the limitations of his ability he is not distressed by the fact that men do not recognize the ability that he has.
author: Confucius

quote: With fools, there is no companionship. Rather than to live with men who are selfish, vain, quarrelsome, and obstinate, let a man walk alone.
author: Buddha

quote: Men are disturbed not by things, but by the view which they take of them.
author: Epictetus

quote: Now the reason the enlightened prince and the wise general conquer the enemy whenever they move and their achievements surpass those of ordinary men is foreknowledge.
author: Sun Tzu

quote: Bad men are full of repentance.
author: Aristotle

quote: There are only two kinds of men: the righteous who think they are sinners and the sinners who think they are righteous.
author: Blaise Pascal

quote: How could man rejoice in victory and delight in the slaughter of men?
author: Lao Tzu

quote: If we know that our own men are in a condition to attack, but are unaware that the enemy is not open to attack, we have gone only halfway towards victory.
author: Sun Tzu

quote: It is unbecoming for young men to utter maxims.
author: Aristotle

quote: There is no such thing as justice in the abstract it is merely a compact between men.
author: Epicurus

quote: When a hundred men stand together, each of them loses his mind and gets another one.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: I will not be concerned at other men's not knowing me I will be concerned at my own want of ability.
author: Confucius

quote: Regarding life, the wisest men of all ages have judged alike: it is worthless.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: Nothing astonishes men so much as common sense and plain dealing.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: Men exist for the sake of one another.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: The world would be happier if men had the same capacity to be silent that they have to speak.
author: Baruch Spinoza

quote: Most men are within a finger's breadth of being mad.
author: Diogenes

quote: Every actual State is corrupt. Good men must not obey laws too well.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: A great value of antiquity lies in the fact that its writings are the only ones that modern men still read with exactness.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: Those who excel in virtue have the best right of all to rebel, but then they are of all men the least inclined to do so.
author: Aristotle

quote: You will not be punished for your anger, you will be punished by your anger.
author: Buddha

quote: When anger rises, think of the consequences.
author: Confucius

quote: Holding on to anger is like grasping a hot coal with the intent of throwing it at someone else you are the one who gets burned.
author: Buddha

quote: The one who cannot restrain their anger will wish undone, what their temper and irritation prompted them to do.
author: Horace

quote: When you are offended at any man's fault, turn to yourself and study your own failings. Then you will forget your anger.
author: Epictetus

quote: Anger is a short madness.
author: Horace

quote: Anger cannot be dishonest.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: Lawyers are men who hire out their words and anger.
author: Horace

quote: There is nothing permanent except change.
author: Heraclitus

quote: If you do not change direction, you may end up where you are heading.
author: Lao Tzu

quote: Change in all things is sweet.
author: Aristotle

quote: Excess generally causes reaction, and produces a change in the opposite direction, whether it be in the seasons, or in individuals, or in governments.
author: Plato

quote: To change ones life: Start immediately. Do it flamboyantly.
author: William James

quote: No change of circumstances can repair a defect of character.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: The universe is change our life is what our thoughts make it.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: If you realize that all things change, there is nothing you will try to hold on to. If you are not afraid of dying, there is nothing you cannot achieve.
author: Lao Tzu

quote: If you believe that feeling bad or worrying long enough will change a past or future event, then you are residing on another planet with a different reality system.
author: William James

quote: Change alone is unchanging.
author: Heraclitus

quote: Win as if you were used to it, lose as if you enjoyed it for a change.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: There was something undifferentiated and yet complete, which existed before Heaven and Earth. Soundless and formless, it depends on nothing and does not change. It operates everywhere and is free from danger. It may be considered the mother of the universe. I do not know its name; I call it Tao.
author: Lao Tzu

quote: The faults of a superior person are like the sun and moon. They have their faults, and everyone sees them; they change and everyone looks up to them.
author: Confucius

quote: It may be that the satisfaction I need depends on my going away, so that when I've gone and come back, I'll find it at home.
author: Rumi

quote: There are a thousand ways to kneel and kiss the ground there are a thousand ways to go home again.
author: Rumi

quote: An artist has no home in Europe except in Paris.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: However much I might try to expound or explain Love, when I come to Love itself, I am ashamed of my explanations... Love alone can explain the mysteries of love and lovers.
author: Rumi

quote: Virtue is not left to stand alone. He who practices it will have neighbors.
author: Confucius

quote: Of those beings who live in ignorance, shut up and confined, as it were, in an egg, I have first broken the eggshell of ignorance and alone in the universe obtained the most exalted, universal Buddhahood.
author: Buddha

quote: If you are lonely when you're alone, you are in bad company.
author: Jean-Paul Sartre

quote: He alone is free who lives with free consent under the entire guidance of reason.
author: Baruch Spinoza

quote: There are two types of poor people, those who are poor together and those who are poor alone. The first are the true poor, the others are rich people out of luck.
author: Jean-Paul Sartre

quote: Every man is born as many men and dies as a single one.
author: Martin Heidegger

quote: Perhaps I know best why it is man alone who laughs he alone suffers so deeply that he had to invent laughter.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: It is the fight alone that pleases us, not the victory.
author: Blaise Pascal

quote: It is not necessary that you leave the house. Remain at your table and listen. Do not even listen, only wait. Do not even wait, be wholly still and alone. The world will present itself to you for its unmasking, it can do no other, in ecstasy it will writhe at your feet.
author: Franz Kafka

quote: Sensual love deceives one as to the nature of heavenly love; it could not do so alone, but since it unconsciously has the element of heavenly love within it, it can do so.
author: Franz Kafka

quote: The Fuhrer alone is the present and future German reality and its law. Learn to know ever more deeply: from now on every single thing demands decision, and every action responsibility.
author: Martin Heidegger

quote: Society, being codified by man, decrees that woman is inferior; she can do away with this inferiority only by destroying the male's superiority.
author: Simone de Beauvoir

quote: To cut short the question of the law of retaliation, we must note that even in its primitive form it can operate only between two individuals of whom one is absolutely innocent, and the other absolutely guilty. The victim, to be sure, is innocent. But can the society that is supposed to represent the victim lay claim to innocence?
author: Albert Camus

quote: The society based on production is only productive, not creative.
author: Albert Camus

quote: Society cares for the individual only so far as he is profitable.
author: Simone de Beauvoir

quote: Justice in the life and conduct of the State is possible only as first it resides in the hearts and souls of the citizens.
author: Plato

quote: It is right to give every man his due.
author: Plato

quote: The chain of wedlock is so heavy that it takes two to carry it - and sometimes three.
author: Heraclitus

quote: The only way to deal with an unfree world is to become so absolutely free that your very existence is an act of rebellion.
author: Albert Camus

quote: A free press can, of course, be good or bad, but, most certainly without freedom, the press will never be anything but bad.
author: Albert Camus

quote: The desire of gold is not for gold. It is for the means of freedom and benefit.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quote: I am not an Athenian or a Greek, but a citizen of the world.
author: Diogenes

quote: Men are never really willing to die except for the sake of freedom: therefore they do not believe in dying completely.
author: Albert Camus

quote: I wish that every human life might be pure transparent freedom.
author: Simone de Beauvoir

quote: Is freedom anything else than the right to live as we wish? Nothing else.
author: Epictetus

quote: Nothing has been purchased more dearly than the little bit of reason and sense of freedom which now constitutes our pride.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: Undeservedly you will atone for the sins of your fathers.
author: Horace

quote: If you think in terms of a year, plant a seed; if in terms of ten years, plant trees; if in terms of 100 years, teach the people.
author: Confucius

quote: Study the past, if you would divine the future.
author: Confucius

quote: Real generosity toward the future lies in giving all to the present.
author: Albert Camus

quote: Look back over the past, with its changing empires that rose and fell, and you can foresee the future, too.
author: Marcus Aurelius

quote: The future influences the present just as much as the past.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: Enjoy present pleasures in such a way as not to injure future ones.
author: Seneca

quote: Cease to inquire what the future has in store, and take as a gift whatever the day brings forth.
author: Horace

quote: In each action we must look beyond the action at our past, present, and future state, and at others whom it affects, and see the relations of all those things. And then we shall be very cautious.
author: Blaise Pascal

quote: All sciences are now under the obligation to prepare the ground for the future task of the philosopher, which is to solve the problem of value, to determine the true hierarchy of values.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quote: A quality is something capable of being completely embodied. A law never can be embodied in its character as a law except by determining a habit. A quality is how something may or might have been. A law is how an endless future must continue to be.
author: Charles Sanders Peirce
